I've mapped out the ligand L1102 atom coordinates and now I'm scanning nearby residues to identify protein atoms within 4 Å of this binding region.

Checking LYS28's CG against O1, I find a distance of about 3.61 Å, so that residue counts as a contact. I also test ARG24's NE against C1 and find roughly 3.61 Å, confirming another qualifying contact, and I'm now checking ARG24's CZ atom as well.

Checking LYS28's CE and NZ atoms against the ligand carbons—CE to C2 comes in at 3.70 which qualifies, and NZ to C2 also fits at 3.46, though NZ to C3 lands just barely outside the cutoff at 4.01.

I confirm LYS28 is close enough via its CG, CE, and NZ atoms. Scanning other residues like GLU31, GLU27, LEU35, LYS38—they're all too far in the x or z direction to matter. That leaves ARG24 and LYS28 as the only qualifying residues, so now I want to double-check LEU25 and SER26 too.

LEU25's atoms sit too far in the positive z direction to count. ARG24's backbone O and CA atoms both fall within range of O1—confirming ARG24 was already correctly counted. LYS23's carbon atom is too far away to matter.

Checking a few more possibilities—LYS28, GLU20, GLU22, LYS19, LEU21, CYS42—none of them come close enough in coordinates. So my final answer stands: A:R24 and A:K28.
